blocks.task_summary: Prove by contradiction that 1/(x(1-x)) ≥ 4 for x ∈ ℝ, 0 < x < 1.
method_path: Multiply by positive x(1-x) to get 1 < 4x(1-x)
accepted_alternatives: Use partial fractions and calculus to find minimum of 1/(x(1-x)) is 4, contradicting assumption <4
Use product rule to differentiate 1/(x(1-x)), find minimum 4, contradicting assumption <4

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: assume that 1/(x(1-x)) < 4 ... attempt to form a quadratic inequality ... 4x^2 - 4x + 1 < 0 ... (2x-1)^2 < 0 ... a contradiction, since (2x-1)^2 ≥ 0
METHOD 2: assume that 1/(x(1-x)) < 4 ... partial fractions ... minimum value is 4 ... a contradiction, since 4 < 4
METHOD 3: assume that 1/(x(1-x)) < 4 ... product rule ... minimum value is 4 ... a contradiction, since 4 < 4
